_metadata.rubric: x04c rubric (backlog of full-strength index combinations; balanced owner standard), 2026-10-19
_metadata.independence: I read only the instructions file and the single input file x04c-re-input.json; no other file, repository search, web or paid API was used.

hints.reason: Classic picnic scene: ants invade the picnic (ANT) and lunch comes in a picnic basket (BASKET); both click instantly.

pairs.pair_note: Textbook scene clue; on a board containing BLANKET or TABLE too, PICNIC becomes ambiguous, so avoid co-locating those pairs.

hints.reason: Picnic scene: ants crash it (ANT) and you spread a picnic blanket (BLANKET); the owner's own example of a welcome scene clue.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; same board-collision caveat as the other PICNIC pairs.

hints.reason: Picnic scene: ants at the picnic (ANT) and the picnic table (TABLE) is a fixed, instantly familiar phrase.

pairs.pair_note: Solid, slightly less vivid than basket/blanket because TABLE has many other homes.

hints.reason: The hoop's net (BASKETBALL) and a fishing net (FISHING) are both everyday images of the word.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, fair; NET also reaches TENNIS and BUTTERFLY, so watch board collisions.

hints.reason: Slam dunk (BASKETBALL) and Grand Slam (TENNIS) are both instantly familiar sports phrases, and it is livelier than the served NET.

pairs.pair_note: Both SLAM and the served NET are good; SLAM is the more satisfying of the two.

hints.reason: Picnic table (TABLE) is direct, and Yogi Bear's 'pic-a-nic basket' (plus bears raiding campsite picnics) reaches BEAR with a moment of thought.

pairs.pair_note: Yogi is older but still widely known; the BEAR side is the softer one.

hints.reason: Birds have wings (BIRD) and buffalo wings are the famous bar food (BUFFALO); the 'buffalo don't have wings' joke makes it a real click.

pairs.pair_note: One of the best in the batch.

hints.reason: Bird wings (BIRD) are instant, but a building wing (HOSPITAL) is one of many WING targets (plane, buffalo, chicken, any large building) and few players would land on hospital; the line also overstates that every department has a wing.
hints.fix: Big hospitals are divided into wings, like the maternity wing.

pairs.pair_note: The idea is fair but flat and HOSPITAL is a weak destination for WING; the department-per-wing line is not accurate.

hints.reason: Wings on birds (BIRD) and planes (PLANE) are correct and instant, but it is an unremarkable shared feature and the served SUPERMAN ('It's a bird! It's a plane!') is clearly the more delightful hint.

pairs.pair_note: Keep SUPERMAN as the served hint; WING adds nothing.

hints.reason: Sonic the blue hedgehog (BLUE) and the sonic boom of a supersonic jet (BOOM) pair a pop-culture icon with a familiar science phrase.

pairs.pair_note: Nice two-route clue; 'Sonic Boom' is also the name of a Sonic spin-off, which only helps.

hints.reason: Sonic is a blue hedgehog (BLUE) who stars in Sega's video games (VIDEO GAME); one character covers both, easy but satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Fine; the explanation is a little repetitive but accurate.

hints.reason: A butterfly net (BUTTERFLY) and a fishing net (FISHING) are both classic catching tools; easy and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Pleasant 'catching things' picture.

hints.reason: Honking a car horn (CAR) versus a goat's horns (GOAT) is a clean, instant double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair.

hints.reason: Car horn (CAR) and a ram's big curled horns (RAM) are both immediate; the curled-horn image makes RAM vivid.

pairs.pair_note: Players may also think of Ram trucks, which only reinforces the CAR side.

hints.reason: A deck of cards (CARD) and the carol 'Deck the Halls' (HALL) use the noun and the verb; both instant, with a real 'oh, nice' moment.

pairs.pair_note: One of the strongest DECK pairs.

hints.reason: Screaming fans at a concert (CONCERT) and an electric fan in summer heat (SUMMER) are a clean, familiar double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair; FAN also reaches STADIUM and HOT, so watch board collisions.

hints.reason: Shrek the ogre's sidekick Donkey (DONKEY) and his famous 'ogres are like onions, they have layers' line (LAYER) make a delightful Shrek callback.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent pop-culture clue; SHREK would also work but OGRE ties more neatly to the quote.

hints.reason: Slamming a door (DOOR) and tennis's Grand Slams (TENNIS) are both instantly familiar uses of the word.

pairs.pair_note: Fair and quick; less fun than the basketball version.

hints.reason: Ogres are stock fairy-tale monsters (FAIRYTALE) and Shrek is the famous ogre (SHREK), whose film is itself a fairy-tale parody.

pairs.pair_note: Easy; SHREK side is almost a definition, but the fairy-tale side makes it a fair two-word clue.

hints.reason: Sonic's speed ('gotta go fast', and 'sonic' itself means sound-speed) covers FAST, and collecting golden rings covers RING.

pairs.pair_note: Good game-world pairing, well known thanks to the films.

hints.reason: A fishing net (FISHING) and the net across a tennis court (TENNIS) are both immediate.

pairs.pair_note: Plain but fair.

hints.reason: Goats have horns (GOAT) and the unicorn is defined by its single horn (UNICORN); easy shared feature with a fun real-vs-mythical contrast.

pairs.pair_note: Easy; HORN reaches several animals, so board context matters.

hints.reason: OGRE points straight at SHREK, but GREEN is reached only through Shrek's own colour (folklore ogres are not green), so the second side is a chain through the first target rather than a property of the hint.

pairs.pair_note: Many players will get it because Shrek made ogres green in the popular mind; genuinely unsure whether that counts as a real click.

hints.reason: 'Deck the Halls' (HALL) and a ship's deck (SHIP) split the verb and noun neatly; both instant.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: 'Deck the Halls' (HALL) is instant, but a skateboard's deck (SKATEBOARD) is skater vocabulary that many general players would not reach from DECK before cards, ships or patios.

pairs.pair_note: Accurate and clicks once explained; the question is whether 'skateboard deck' is familiar enough for the general audience.

hints.reason: An electric fan on a hot day (HOT) and sports fans packing a stadium (STADIUM) are both immediate meanings.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair.

hints.reason: Sailor's knots (KNOT) are a familiar phrase and sailors live at sea (SEA); easy, with 'knots' as nautical speed as a bonus.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair.

hints.reason: Sailor's knots (KNOT) and sailors aboard ships (SHIP) are both immediate.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair.

hints.reason: A lightning bolt (LIGHTNING) versus nuts-and-bolts hardware alongside screws (SCREW) is a crisp, satisfying double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: Bolting/deadbolting a door (LOCK) and bolts alongside screws in the toolbox (SCREW) are both familiar hardware meanings.

pairs.pair_note: Fair but less lively than LIGHTNING + SCREW since both sides are hardware.

hints.reason: Sailors at sea (SEA) is direct and the anime title Sailor Moon (MOON) is a fun, widely known name even to non-viewers; TIDE is a more universal alternative but SAILOR is not unremarkable.

pairs.pair_note: TIDE (the moon pulls the tides of the sea) is the obvious science hint and would also PASS; SAILOR is the more playful one.

hints.reason: Sailors aboard ships (SHIP) is direct and Sailor Moon (MOON) is a widely known anime title, giving a playful click.

pairs.pair_note: Relies on Sailor Moon name recognition; older players may need the explanation.

hints.reason: Poetry slam (POETRY) and Grand Slam (TENNIS) are both familiar fixed phrases, and the pairing of poets with tennis is a pleasant surprise.

pairs.pair_note: Poetry slam is well known in the U.S., though slightly less universal than slam dunk.

hints.reason: A ram's curled horns (RAM) and a unicorn's single horn (UNICORN) are both defining features.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair.

hints.reason: Sports fans packing a stadium (STADIUM) and a cooling fan in summer (SUMMER) are both immediate meanings.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair.
